question: Can mandatory overlapping shortcuts constrain unbound surface syntax when their literal A/B/C drawings need never occur?
hypothesis_to_check: For every finite surface alphabet of size2..25, assign any two distinct observed types to MU=AB and NU=BC; inject all remaining at most23 types into literal D..Z; reserve literal A/B/C as unobserved. Every word then reencodes identically under either left-first or right-first priority.
scope: Source-free formal construction. No new Voynich query, native fit, language identification or glyph key. Existing G1 counts are only a conditional applicability limit, not a proved manuscript alphabet.
proof_obligations: All cross-atom boundaries avoid a new AB or BC match
Both internal shortcut matches survive either scanning order
Every role and repetition including repeated shortcuts covered
Both shortcuts may actually occur; their inactivity must not be required
Retain ABC overlap distinction when literal A/C is bound and observed
checks: Short direct encoders in each direction plus all words up to length6 over MU,NU and one representative ordinary literal; per-type substitution covers the other ordinary literal labels. Deductive proof, not finite enumeration, carries all-length claim.

decisions.proof_holds: Do not select933 or scan the corpus solely for legal coverage. A useful continuation needs a justified literal/shortcut binding or explicit source/content distribution; do not require a confirmed word.
decisions.proof_fails: Record exact boundary countercase; reconsider whether the distinguishing syntax can support a small fixed test before any corpus implementation.

predecessors: GDT608 directed partial composition does not prove a writer
GDT995 already uses mandatory forward compatibility with supplied literal maps; its nonoverlapping suffix orders remain equal
GDT883 tests overlapping consumed blocks, not disjoint shortcut consumption
assumptions: Two distinct shortcut drawings, all literals distinct
No corpus-wide requirement that every literal drawing occurs
